author: grand canyon times
title: Ninth grader Arhaan Shah earns national recognition for AidSense app in technology competition
text:
Arhaan Shah, a ninth grade student and CREST participant, was recognized nationally on May 5 for his work in technology and computer science. Shah was invited to present his award-winning app, AidSense, in Washington, D.C., after earning honors in the Congressional App Challenge.
The Congressional App Challenge is one of the nation’s leading competitions for student developers. Shah’s achievement highlights the importance of supporting young innovators who use technology to address real-world problems.
Shah said, “In our communities, many people struggle to find local resources or look for the answers to their questions about a specific place. There is a high demand for supportive services, shelters, and resource access, yet awareness and access are limited in underserved neighborhoods.” He added that “AidSense helps users quickly and confidently find the support they need, overall making the process significantly easier.”
His project was selected from among many student submissions nationwide. As part of his recognition, he will have an opportunity to showcase his work before members of Congress and leaders from the technology community. He will also present near the White House as part of event activities.
Paradise Valley Unified School District serves the Paradise Valley area in Arizona and operates under a board of school trustees. The district promotes anti-racism, equity, inclusion policies and practices; focuses on engaging students through quality instruction; offers community learning centers; magnet programs; and specializes in public schooling according to its official website.
Shah’s participation demonstrates how local students can advance their skills through programs like CREST while contributing meaningful solutions at both local and national levels.
